cases.explain: «Доброе имя» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.

cases.explain: «великих богатств» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.

cases.explain: «верный путь» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

cases.explain: «чужой жены» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit. He who is under Yahweh’s wrath will fall into it.

cases.explain: «глубокая яма» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit. He who is under Yahweh’s wrath will fall into it.

cases.explain: «верным словам» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: To teach you truth, reliable words, to give sound answers to the ones who sent you?

cases.explain: «древней межи» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone which your fathers have set up.
